result.summary: An 84-year-old tenant who lives alone with a heart condition has had no heating or hot water for over 3 days in cold weather, and now feels dizzy. The landlord hasn't replied to 3 emails and is away until 20 Oct. I treated this as emergency safety work, which landlord approval does not block. I texted the tenant with safety advice, texted the landlord's mobile, and escalated to ops at high priority for a welfare call and same-day engineer dispatch. I moved the stage to provider_selection, recorded profile facts, and set a 6-hour follow-up.
result.situation: The heating failed on 6 Oct (boiler display blank, 3C overnight). Approval was requested on 6 Oct and chased on 7 and 8 Oct, but the landlord only sent an out-of-office reply. On 9 Oct the tenant reported still no heating and dizziness. There is no contractor on file and no pre-approved limit.

judgement.why_this_decision: Under emergency rules, a vulnerable tenant with no heating in cold weather is an emergency, and approval does not block safety work. Event 006's dizziness adds a possible medical risk. Classifiers: severity emergency 1.0, safety 0.94, reply needs a human 0.95. I couldn't assign a contractor because none is on the ticket or in the property history, so dispatch and the welfare call need a human. Two chases have passed with no landlord reply, which is also a reason to escalate.

alternatives_considered.why_not: Landlord is away until 20 Oct; the tenant's health is at risk now.
No contractor is named in the records, and inventing one would break the rules. Ops must pick a Gas Safe engineer.
Approval isn't needed for emergency work, and a pending approval could look like a blocker. I texted the landlord's mobile instead and asked ops to call.

checks_performed: Loaded full ticket context: no holds, approvals, contractor or property history
Classified the tenant SMS (review, safety 0.87) and the intake (emergency, emergency_dispatch)
Confirmed there is no pre-approved spend limit on the landlord's profile
Landlord was emailed 3 times and sent an out-of-office (event 005)
Outbound guard blocked the first landlord SMS; I rewrote it to remove the implied booking and resent it successfully
assumptions: The estimate of up to £200 (event 002) is still a reasonable figure for the emergency call-out
The landlord's mobile in event 005 is current

intake → provider_selection (emergency work, approval not blocking)

escalation.reason: Vulnerable 84-year-old tenant has had no heating for 3+ days, now feels dizzy, and the landlord can't be reached
escalation.handover_summary: 6 Primrose Court R/13: Mr Finch (84, heart condition, walking frame, lives alone) has had no heating or hot water since 6 Oct and is now dizzy. Landlord is away until 20 Oct and silent after 3 emails. Tenant and landlord have been texted. No contractor is on file.
escalation.recommendation: Phone the tenant now for a welfare check and push 999/111 if he is still dizzy. Send a Gas Safe engineer today as emergency work, within about £200. Supply temporary heaters if needed. Phone the landlord on 07700 900456. Consider a welfare referral and contacting his daughter.
